name: Gold Leaf
desc: Gilding laid over the scene in overlapping courses — beaten leaf with torn deckle edges, the lap lines showing where each sheet crosses the last, holidays left open so the picture underneath still reads, loose skewings tumbling through the air, and an agate burnisher travelling past that lights each course as it goes.

coverage.doc: how many courses actually took — the misses are holidays that let the scene through

scale.doc: size of each beaten leaf against the frame

energy.doc: how hard the burnished leaf ignites as the agate passes

density.doc: skewings in the air, and the reach of the burnisher

hue.doc: the metal (45 = true 23k gold; ~30 reads copper)

speed.doc: rate of the burnisher pass and the drift of the skewings

x.doc: where the burnisher is working, across the frame

y.doc: where the burnisher is working, up the frame

alpha.doc: overlay opacity — kept off full by default so the scene reads through the gilding

style.doc: gold: 23k water gilding, warm and opulent over red bole · moon_gold: pale cool white gold · copper: schlagmetal, warmer and already going over · graphite: lead and graphite foil, sombre and near-monochrome · setout: non-representational — the gilder's setting-out, flat tinted planes and hard linework, no metal or sheen at all

act.doc: lay: courses go down and the skewings drift · burnish: the agate works hard across the gilding, igniting it in sequence · shed: the gilding is failing — leaves lift, blow away and leave holidays

seed.doc: re-gilds — new courses, torn edges, holidays and skewings
